title: Unbounded queues, timers, retries, or object retention in a TypeScript runtime
preconditions: attacker-controlled requests schedule retained work or objects
dangerous_transitions: untrusted work is enqueued without a count/byte/time budget
failure triggers unbounded retry or retained callbacks
sink_semantics: arrays/maps/queues, timers, promises, worker queues, and buffered streams
counterevidence: Queue, concurrency, retention, and retry budgets are enforced before admitting work and on failure paths.
verification_recipe: Identify the retaining owner and every enqueue, retry, cancellation, and drain transition.
Measure queue depth and retained memory with bounded and adversarial-rate controls.
